document.title: Smt Lakshmi Devi (Also Referred As Laxmi ... vs Sh Gajinder Singh on 10 February, 2020

raw_text:
1. Plaintiff has filed suit for cancellation, declaration and permanent injunction.
2. It is the case of the plaintiff that she is Bhumidar in possession of land bearing khasra no. 43/12(3-17); 13(4-16); 14 (4-
16); 15(1-14); 17(3-19); 18(4-16); 19 (5-03); 23/1 (3 -08) and 43/28 (0-3) in all measuring 32 bighas and 12 biswas situated within the revenue estate of Ghuman Hera, Delhi, [hereinafter to called as "Suit Land"]
3. It is the case of the plaintiff that subject matter of the dispute pertains to the land comprising in Khasra no. 43/14 (4-16) and information was received that defendant no.1 has executed a sale deed in favour of defendant no.2 on 14.11.1996 purporting to be acted as General Attorney of plaintiff in respect of land comprising in Khasra no. 43/14 (4-16), [hereinafter to be called as "Land in Dispute"]
4. It is also averred that the power of attorney was registered in the office of Sub Registrar office on 19.07.1996 and sale deed being CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 2 / 45 document No.14619 in Addl Book No.1, Volume No. 8603 at page 9 to 17 was executed on 14.11.1996 by defendant no.1 in favour of defendant no.2 who was an Ex Tehsildar of Mahrauli Tehsil.
5. It is further averred that land bearing khasra no. 43/12( 3-
17); 13(4-16); 14 (4-16); 15(1-4); 17(3-19); 18(4-16); 19 (5-03); 23/1 (3 -08) and 43/28 (0-3) in all measuring 32 bighas and 12 biswas situated within the revenue estate of Ghuman Hera, Delhi was alienated by the defendant No. 1 through separate sale deed and in this respect plaintiff was advised to file separate suits in respect of portion of land as mentioned in suit land in different sale deed.
6. It is also averred that on the basis of the sale deed the defendant no 1 and 2 have got the mutation in respect of the land without the knowledge of plaintiff. Mutation entries in respect of different sale deeds were sanctioned on 13.01.1997. It is averred that plaintiff did not receive single penny as consideration from any of the defendants.
7. It is also stated that at no stage of time plaintiff had contemplated to sell/ alienate her land through the agency of defendant no 1 or anybody else and it was also averred that defendant no 1 was never appointed as power of attorney on behalf of plaintiff.
8. It is further averred that plaintiff came to know through her CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 3 / 45 husband in the last week of September 1997 that the land as referred above was sold by the defendant No. 1 in favour of defendant no. 2 and entries were also made in the revenue record.
9. It is also averred that when husband of plaintiff became aware about the factum of mutation, he(husband of plaintiff) inspected the relevant revenue record and informed the plaintiff that mutation order in respect of the land in question has been passed and after getting information with to mutation of "suit land", an appeal was filed in respect of grant of sanction of mutation, appeal was before Deputy Commissioner, Kapashera and same is still pending. The plaintiff was also advised to file a suit for declaration, cancellation of the deed of attorney and sale deed on the basis of which the name of the defendant no 2 stands substituted as Bhumidar of plaintiff's land as mentioned in para no. 1 of the plaint.
10. Suit has been filed to get the sale deed as null and void and for setting aside mutation order dated 13.01.1997 as null and void ab initio.
11. It is pleaded that plaintiff is a simple illiterate housewife and has nothing to do with the worldly affair and defendant no 1 was treated like a son being the younger brother of husband and she never had any intention to appoint Defendant No.1 as her power of attorney. It is also stated that the contents of General Power of Attorney (GPA) CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 4 / 45 were not explained to defendant no.1 as she is not conversant with the English and signature appearing on the document were procured under the impression as if she is filing an application for sanction of mutation in respect of suit land. It is also stated that plaintiff did not put her thumb mark on deed of attorney under the impression that she is putting the same on the application for sanction of mutation of her land purchased in April 1996.
12. It is also averred that plaintiff was deceived by defendant no 1 as regards to actual nature and contents of deed of attorney and therefore, the alleged deed of attorney executed by plaintiff in favour of defendant no 1 is nullity and not binding on the plaintiff.
13. It is also averred that defendant no 3 was impleaded as party to the suit on the ground as per the recitals in the sale deed is that plaintiff had entered into an agreement for sale with confirming party vide agreement to sell dated 24.07.1996 and the plaintiff has received a consideration of Rs 495000/-. It is also asserted that no agreement to sell was entered by plaintiff with defendant no 3 or anyone else. It is also averred that defendant no 3 is totally unknown to the plaintiff. Plaintiff has also casted doubt on the recitals made in the sale deed.
14. An objection was also raised by the plaintiff that mutation entry was wrongly made by Tehseeldar since no notice was served on the plaintiff and it was submitted that the entire proceedings were CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 5 / 45 done at the instance of defendant no 2 without inviting any objection on plaintiff.
15. It is also averred that proclamation was not made in terms of mandatory provision of Delhi Land Revenue Act . The plaintiff has also challenged the proclamation issued under the signature of Tehsildar on 27.12.1996.
16. It is further averred that plaintiff was totally kept in dark with regard to the mutation proceedings due to which she could not file her objection. It is also pleaded that the order of mutation was illegal, void and without jurisdiction and liable to be set aside and declared as null and void.
17. It is also stated that plaintiff is in possession of the land in dispute although name of defendant no 2 is recorded as Bhumidar in the column no. 3 of Khasra Girdawari. It is also averred that on the basis of wrong entries in the revenue record showing defendant no 2 in possession and defendant no.2 is threatening to take the possession of the plaintiff over the suit land.
18. The plaintiff on the basis of aforesaid facts prayed for cancellation of sale deed and also for declaring the mutation dated 13.01.1997 in respect of khasra no. 43/14 measuring 4 bighas 16 biswas in case no. 861/TNG/96-97 sanctioning mutation in the name CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 6 / 45 of defendant no 2 as not binding on the plaintiff and for declaration it be declared as null and void.
19. The plaintiff has also prayed for the decree of cancellation, of Sale Deed executed in favour of defendant no.2 by defendant no.1. Plaintiff also prayed for decree of permanent injunction for restraining defendant no 2 from creating third party right in respect of subject matter of dispute and for interfering in the peaceful possession of plaintiff.
WRITTEN STATEMENT ON BEHALF OF DEFENDANT NO.1
20. Defendant no.1 filed the Written Statement by taking number of preliminary objections that suit filed by plaintiff is not maintainable and same was filed with an intention to pressurize defendants and the suit filed by the plaintiff also does not conform to the requirements of Order 6 rule 4 CPC . It was also prayed that suit has not been valued properly for the purposes of court fees and jurisdiction.
21. On merits, defendant no 1 denied the averments as made in the plaint and contented that suit land including the land in dispute was sold for Rs 13.5 lakhs. It was denied that plaintiff did not execute power of attorney in favour of defendant no 1. It is also stated that confirming parties i.e. defendant no 3 and others entered into an CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 7 / 45 agreement with plaintiff through one Sh Mahinder Singh, S/o Bhagwan Singh, R/o H No 151, Village Nilothi who is the relative of plaintiff and answering defendant. It is also pleaded that plaintiff had executed General power of attorney in favour of answering defendant after receiving the entire consideration. The deed writer prepared General Power of Attorney (GPA) on the instructions of plaintiff and her husband Pratap Singh. It is also pleaded that the deed writer typed GPA on non judicial stamp paper and also explained the contents of GPA to the plaintiff in presence of her husband and the husband of plaintiff also read the contents of GPA. It is also averred that Mahinder Singh also asked plaintiff and her husband to execute a Will in favour of answering defendant and both plaintiff and her husband had agreed to execute the Will and all the above documents were presented before the Office of Sub Registrar after explaining the contents of GPA and Will to the plaintiff in the presence of her husband. It is also pleaded that actual and physical possession of land was handed over to defendant no 3 and other parties through defendant no 1 and Mahinder Singh.
22. It is also stated that entire transaction and mutation was in the complete knowledge of plaintiff since the beginning.
23. In para no. 4 of Written Statement, defence was taken that after execution and registration of sale deed in favour of defendant no. 2 by answering defendant no 1 as an attorney of plaintiff, the relation CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 8 / 45 in between defendant no 1 and husband of plaintiff were strained because of filing of the false cases by the husband of plaintiff. Allegations were also made that husband of plaintiff had filed false FIR against defendant no 1 in PS Najafgarh on the allegation that signature of husband of plaintiff was forged by defendant no 1 and upon the examination of the said documents it was revealed that signature were of the husband of plaintiff and allegations against defendant no 1 were false and bogus.
24. Defendant no 1 denied that plaintiff is the simple illiterate housewife and took a stand that she has been purchasing the illegal property since 1980 and appearing before various authorities including Sub Registrar for execution and registration of sale deeds of immoveable properties. It is also averred that plaintiff holds bank account in various banks and is undertaking monetary transaction for considerable length of time and thus can easily understand the wordly affairs. It is also averred that husband of plaintiff is a highly educated person and the son of plaintiff is major and both of them are undertaking the business of sale and purchase of property. Defendant No.1 also took an argumentative defence that if any fraud was committed by answering defendant then plaintiff would have very well exposed to her husband. The defendant No. 1 also denied the allegation that the thumb impression affixed on the General Power of Attorney(GPA) by the plaintiff by treating the same for the purposes of mutation. It is further submitted that after execution and registration CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 9 / 45 of sale deeds in favour of defendant no 2 by the answering defendant No.1 as an attorney of the plaintiff, some family dispute arose between husband of plaintiff and answering defendant No.1 sometime in the month of March 1997 due to which relations between the husband of plaintiff and the answering defendant became strained due to false and frivolous cases initiated by the husband of plaintiff against the answering defendant. Husband of plaintiff is a person of suspicious character and manipulator. It is also relevant hereto point out that the husband of plaintiff also lodged a false and frivolous FIR against the defendant No.1 at PS Najafgarh, Delhi alleging therein that the defendant no.1 had forged his signatures on the some papers to deprive him from property. On the orders of court, documents were examined by the expert and competent expert opined that the signature in documents were of husband of plaintiff and the complaint was found to be false and bogus. It was also pointed that in one of the civil suit, husband of plaintiff denied his signatures on registered documents and submitted that these instances clearly indicate the conduct and behaviour of the plaintiff's husband in making false and frivolous allegations. Plaintiff's allegation that she was not aware either he factum of execution of the power of attorney or the sale deed was denied. It was asserted that suit is filed by plaintiff under pressure, coercion and at the instance of her husband. The entire allegation in the plaint are false and frivolous and concocted even to the knowledge of the plaintiff and her husband.
25. Contents of paragraph to that plaintiff is a simple illiterate housewife confined to her house and does not know much about the worldly affair were denied and it was pointed that the plaintiff has been purchasing the immoveable properties since 1980 onwards. The plaintiff many times appeared before the various authorities including Sub Registrar for the execution and registration of sale deed of the immoveable properties. The plaintiff has been maintaining her separate and independent bank account in various banks. The plaintiff is capable of doing the monetary transaction and can easily understand the worldly affairs. The plaintiff has been living with her husband who is a highly educated person and her elder son also major and doing the business of sale and purchase of properties. It is also contended that if any fraud was committed then she would have exposed it to her husband. The time gap between the execution and registration of power of attorney and the sale deed is about 4 months. It is further denied that the plaintiff had put her thumb mark on the deed of attorney under the impression that she is putting the same on the application for sanction of mutation of her land purchase by her in the month of April 1996. It is also contended that original vendors from whom the plaintiff purchased the property have executed special power of attorney for mutation.
26. It is also averred that contents of General Power of Attorney (GPA) were explained to plaintiff in Hindi and the said power of attorney was executed with free will and consent for executing a CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 11 / 45 registered sale deed in favour of confirming party or their nominee. It is contending that the answering defendant No. 1 has explained the each and every fact and circumstances and the manner in which the power of attorney was executed by the plaintiff in favour of defendant No.1 and it is further averred that amongst all the brothers, the husband of plaintiff is most qualified and literate person, and family members used to seek his advise on important family matters and he has been controlling the entire family affairs.
27. It is also averred that appeal against the mutation order is pending before Deputy Commissioner, South- West, Delhi and the entire allegation with regard to lapses was denied. It is also stated that mutation was sanctioned in accordance with law.
28. In response to the paragraph no.12 of the plaint to the effect that plaintiff is in possession of the suit property was denied by defendant no.1 and it was also stated that the averment in the plaint to the effect that Halka Patwari is not recording the name of plaintiff is incorrect as the amendment in Delhi Land Rules were quashed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the year 1995. Defendant no.1 prayed for the dismissal of the suit.
WRITTEN STATEMENT ON BEHALF OF DEFENDANT NO.2
29. Defendant No.2 filed the separate Written Statement in CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 12 / 45 which dismissal of the suit was prayed and it was contended that defendant no.2 is a bonafide purchaser against consideration and is having protection of law. It is also averred that the present suit is outcome of dispute in between defendant no.1 and plaintiff and suit is liable to be dismissed under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC . It is also averred that plaintiff has filed the suit to extract money and plaintiff was aware about the entire facts.
30. On merits, it is contended on behalf of defendant no.2 that entire Suit Land were sold by plaintiff and as such, defendant no.2 is the owner of the property. It is also stated that no other person except defendant no.2 has right and interest in the suit land. It was denied that there was any fraudulent execution of sale deed and it was also stated that sale deed was rightly executed and defendant no.2 is the bonafide purchaser against consideration. It is also stated that plaintiff is having knowledge that the property was sold by defendant no.1 to defendant no.2 on the basis of the General Power of Attorney executed by plaintiff. It is also averred that it is within the knowledge of plaintiff that when a property is sold then mutation would be granted in favour of the purchaser. It is also stated that registered document on record establishes that land in dispute was sold against consideration. The assertion of non payment of consideration was denied. It was denied that plaintiff never had an intention of selling or alienating the land through agency of defendant no.1 or anybody else as asserted in the plaint. Defendant no.2 also stated that plaintiff has appeared before CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 13 / 45 Sub-Registrar at the execution of the power of attorney and therefore as per Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act, presumption is raised that an official acts are rightly and correctly done. Defendant no.2 also questioned the knowledge of plaintiff that she became aware about the sale of property in the last week of September 1997 as plaintiff was aware about the sale of agricultural land since inception. It was denied that plaintiff came to know about the execution of General power of attorney and sale deed through her husband and on the contrary, it was asserted that plaintiff is having the complete knowledge of the same. It is also stated that mutation was correctly sanctioned in favour of defendant and also averred that mutation is only a formality and same is basically required for the purposes of collecting the land revenue. It is also stated that right and title in favour of a person comes through a registered instrument/ document and all rights in respect of the property came to be possessed by defendant No.2 on the basis of registered sale deed and therefore, question of filing an appeal before Deputy Collector against mutation when there is an existence of sale deed. Defendant also stated that plaintiff has played fraud with the process of Court and has cheated and manipulated all facts to suit her own convenience. It was vehemently denied that defendant is a illiterate housewife or she is not much aware about the worldly affairs. It was denied that plaintiff put a thumb mark on Genenal Power of Attorney attorney construing the same to be an application for sanction of mutation of land purchased in the month of April 1996 by demonstrating that plaintiff has moved CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 14 / 45 separate application before Tehsildar for mutation of land in her favour and application for mutation was moved in the month of September 1996 whereas power of attorney was registered on 19.07.1996. It is also stated that the application for mutation before Tehsildar bear her signature. It was also pointed out that plaintiff had taken contradictory stand as on the one hand, she is claiming herself to be an illiterate lady whereas she is putting signature on various documents. Defendant has also pointed out various transactions which were carried out by plaintiff i.e. (i) operating number of accounts by using her signature (ii) for last 18-20 years, plaintiff has entered into number of transaction which are in Crores of Rupees. It is also possible that she has been filing her return before Income Tax authority to show the income which she could have earned and therefore, assertion of the plaintiff that she is a simpleton and illiterate cannot be believed.
31. It is also stated that plaintiff also used to issue cheque books. It was also pointed out that it is well known fact that Sub-Registrar office at INA deals with the registration of documents and has no concern with the mutation and mutation is only done by a Tehsildar and plaintiff has been conducting sale and purchase of properties for last 20 years and therefore, it is quite logical that she would have appeared before various authorities such as Tehsildar. It is also stated that the entire proceedings/present suit is filed at the behest of husband of plaintiff who is using the plaintiff and furthermore family CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 15 / 45 of plaintiff is engaged in the business of property for number of years and due to which plaintiff is operating number of bank account and therefore, she is having the knowledge of the transaction. Defendant is denied the averment that since plaintiff is not aware about the English language and so she is not aware about its contents and in this regard, it was stated in the Written Statement that documents before office of Sub-Registrar are drafted in English language and plaintiff has been purchasing land on the basis of the documents written in English language. It was also pleaded that things which are done before the office of Sub-registrar is deemed to be done in accordance with law. Allegations with regard to the process of execution of power of attorney questioned by plaintiff were denied and it was stated that plaintiff has narrated things as per her own convenience. It was denied that there was collusion in between defendant no.1, 2 and 3. It was asserted that defendant has purchased the property in proper manner. Assertion with regard to denial of signing of agreement to sell dated 24.07.1996 with defendant no.3 was strongly rebutted by defendant. Plaintiff has also stated that both registering authority and revenue authority have conducted the proceeding wherein name of defendant no.2 was recorded as owner of the property. Defendant denied that plaintiff was not aware about the mutation proceedings. It is averred that since plaintiff is in possession of the property so, his name is rightly reflected in the Khasra Giridawari.
WRITTEN STATEMENT FILED ON BEHALF OF DEFENDANT NO. 3
32. It is averred that suit filed by plaintiff is not maintainable as allegations are false and defamatory. Material Facts were concealed by plaintiff in the plaint.
33. On merits, Defendant No. 3 denied the assertion made in the plaint and averred that "Suit Land" was sold by plaintiff through her attorney. It is also averred that defendant No. 2 is in possession of land. It is also stated that defendant no 3 is associated with one Sh Mahinder Singh who is in the business of sale and purchase of immovable property and defendant no. 3 has authorised Mahinder Singh negotiate with plaintiff and her husband for purchase of suit land. It is also averred that consideration was paid to the plaintiff through Mahinder Singh and after receipt of full and final consideration, plaintiff executed agreement to sell to show it prospective buyer and it is after execution of agreement to sell the answering defendant had purchased the land in question from plaintiff. It is also stated that plaintiff has executed General Power of Attorney in favour of defendant no 1 to execute sale deed in favour of defendant no 3 or its nominee.
34. Remaining allegations made in the plaint were denied and it was asserted that plaintiff is aware about the entire transaction since CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 17 / 45 inception and present suit is basically an outcome of the family dispute in between the husband of plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and other assertions were made in written statement which are in line with the stand taken in the Written Statement filed on behalf of Defendant No.1. In Written Statement, it is further averred that plaintiff has voluntarily entered in the transaction. Prayer Clauses as made in the plaint were denied and it is stated that plaintiff is not entitled for the relief.
35. Plaintiff filed replication to the Written Statement wherein the contents of written statement were denied and those of plaint were reiterated. In replication to the written statement of Defendant No.1, Plaintiff denied that defendant no.3 and others entered into an agreement with plaintiff through Mahinder Singh son of Sh Bhagwan Singh, R/o Village Nilothi. Plaintiff denied that any agreement to sell was executed in between the parties and plaintiff also denied that there was any negotiation in respect of the sale of 32 bighas and 12 biswa. It was reiterated that no consideration was received by plaintiff and further averments in the replication are basically reiteration of the stand taken in the plaint.
36. Replication filed on behalf of plaintiff to the written statement of defendant no 2 is reiteration of stand taken in the plaint. It was denied that there was no action in favour of plaintiff. Plaintiff asserted that she did not execute the Power of Attorney and never CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 18 / 45 appointed Defendant No.1 as Power of Attorney and defendant no.1 was younger brother of husband of plaintiff and various other allegations were made in the Replication and contents of written Statement were denied.
37. Plaintiff filed replication to the Written Statement of Defendant No.3 wherein the contents of written statement were denied and those of plaint were reiterated and stand taken in replication is on same line as that of plaint and it is on the same lines with the stand taken in replication of defendant no.1 and 2.
Miscellaneous proceedings:-
38. Application for amendment dated 22.08.2003, wherein prayer for relief of cancellation of GPA dated 19.07.1996 was dropped and application for amendment was allowed vide order dated 22.12.2003. Pursuant thereto, amended plaint was filed by plaint.
Thereafter, at the stage of final arguments, application under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC was filed on behalf of plaintiff in which amendment was sought in the plaint by which prayer for cancellation of GPA dated 19.07.1996 was prayed, however said application for amendment was dismissed by a detailed order on 01.08.2019. During the pendency of the suit, defendant no.2 expired and his legal heirs were substituted on 20.12.2016. Order of Substitution of LRs of defendant as upheld in CM (M) No.28717 vide order dated CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 19 / 45 14.03.2017 by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi Issues
39. Upon completion of pleadings, vide order dated 18.09.2017, following issues were framed:-
PW-4 Sh Anchint Kumar Bibhanshu, LDC, Gr IV, Reader to DC, South-West has brought the summoned record ie file M No. 861/TNG/96-97 titled as A S Gaur and Laxmi Devi and file M No.857/TNG/96-97 with appeal file bearing no.561/97 titled as Laxmi Devi Vs. A S Gaur , photocopy of the same are Ex.PW4/1 to Ex.PW4/3 respectively (OSR).

41. Evidence on behalf of defendant no.1 and 3 In support of the case, defendant examined DW1 Smt Sarita Gautam, O/o Sub Registrar INA, Vikas Sadan, New Delhi DW3 Sh Sevaji, Record Attendant, Govt of NCT Delhi, Department of Delhi was examined who has brought the original summoned record I.e sale deed dated 10.01.1986 executed by Jamana Das in favour of Smt Laxmi Devi W/o Sh Pratap Singh in respect of CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 21 / 45 the land bearing khasra no 23/15/3, 24/10, 11of Village Mehrauli registered document no 230 Book No 1, Vol No 5406 pages 138 registered (b) Sale deed dated 16.05.1985 executed by Sh Rattan Singh in favour of Laxmi Devi W/o Sh Pratap Singh in respect of the land bearing khasra no 23/16/2, 17, 18/1 of Village Mehrauli, new Delhi registered document No 3611 , Book No. 1, Volume no 5266 pages 189 to 192 registered on 16.05.1985 (c) Sale deed dated 19.11.1995 registered document No 9562 , Book No. 1, Volume no 8943 pages 59-67 registered on 09.11.1995. (d) Sale deed dated 19.11.1995 registered document No 9550 , Book No. 1, Volume no 8942 pages 152-160 registered on 09.11.1995 (e) Sale deed dated 19.11.1995 registered document No 9522 , Book No. 1, Volume no 8944 pages 131-137 registered on 09.11.1995, copy of same are Ex.DW3/1 to Ex.DW3/5.
DW4 Sh Mahender Singh was examined by way of affidavit Ex.DW4/A. DW5 Sh Gajender Singh was also examined by way of affidavit Ex.DW5/A and rely upon documents mark A to mark F however documents mark C already exhibited as EX.DW3/4, mark D already exhibited as Ex.DW3/4 and mark E already exhibited as Ex.DW3/5.
DW-6 Sh Shashank Yadav, Customer Assistant SBI,Vasant Kunj Branch, Delhi who has brought the certified copy of bank opening form of Smt Laxmi Devi bearing old /ac no. 9501, same is Ex.DW6/1.
DW-7 Sh Arvind Chopra, Tehsildar, SDM office, Saket has brought the case file no. 576/8687 and certified copy of same is Ex.DW7/1 and mutation application is at page no.07 (OSR) Defendant Evidence was closed on behalf of defendant no.1 and 3 was closed on 10.05.2018.
42. Evidence on behalf of defendant no.2 On behalf of defendant no.2, D2W1 Sh Sanjay Kumar Gaur was examined by way of affidavit Ex.D2W1/A and relied upon copy of four sale deeds all dated 09.04.1996 executed by earlier owner in favour of plaintiff Laxmi Devi, same are Ex.DW2/1 (Colly, 16 pages).
DE on behalf of defendant no.2 was closed vide order dated 24.05.2018.
43. I have heard Ld counsel for the defendants and perused the written submission filed on behalf of defendants. Despite several opportunities, plaintiff did not advance any arguments.
Ld Counsel for defendant no 1 and 3 has relied upon judgments which are as : 1. Fateh Singh vs Raj Karan & Ors LPA No. 272/2011, 2. Kishan Khandare Vs Kausalyabai & Ors (2007)3 Civ CC 798, 3. Iqbal Ahlmad Vs Naimul in Appeal no. 230/1987 dated 02.04.2004, 4. Shivdas Loknathsingh and ors vs Gayabai Shankar Surwases (1993)MhLj 1623 dated 14.02.1992, 5. Bapu and anr vs Lakhha Banjara Deceased through LR's (2005)30AIC CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 23 / 45 934 dated 13.12.2004, 6. Kanwarani Madna Vati and anr vs Raghunath Singh and ors AIR 1976 HP41 dated 07.10.1975, 7. Koli & ors vs Piru Ram and anr AIR 2008(NOC)808(HP) dated 05.10.2007, 8. 44. Ld counsel for Ld counsel for defendant no 2 has relied upon the judgments which are as: 1.Vimal Chand Ghevas Chand Jain & Ors vs Ramkant Eknath Jadoo (2009)5SCC713, 2. Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti Sahaswan, District Badaun vs Bipin Kumar and Anr (2004)2SCC 283, 3. Karan Madan and ors vs Nageshwar Pandey 2009(2014)DLT241, 4. Devender Kumar Bhardwaj vs Yogesh Chander Bhardwaj 2013 Law Suit(Del)4130 CS No 584/13, 5. Ramaswamy by LR's vbs M. Lobo through LR's (2001)10SCC176, 6. 45. My issuewise finding is as hereunder:-
46. Order VI Rule 4 of CPC provides that where plaintiff pleads misrepresentation, fraud, breach of trust, wilful default or undue influence and any of other cases in which particulars may be necessary beyond such as are exemplified in the aforesaid forms, particulars shall be stated in the pleadings.
47. In Ranganayakamma and another Vs. K.S. Prakash (dead) by LRs. and others; (2008) 15 Supreme Court Cases 673, the Supreme Court after referring to the provisions contained in Order VI Rule 4 of the CPC held that when a fraud is alleged, the particulars thereof are required to be pleaded. It was observed that when a contract is said to be voidable by reason of any coercion, misrepresentation or fraud, the particulars thereof are required to be pleaded.
48. In Ramesh B. Desai Vs. Bipin Vadilal Mehta ; (2006) 5 SCC 638, it was observed that Order VI Rule 4 of CPC requires that complete particulars of fraud shall be stated in the pleadings.
49. Section 17 of Contract Act, 1872 defines fraud and in order to make out a case on the ground of fraud, following ingredients have to be satisfied:
50. In light of the above judgments, Order VI rule 4 CPC and also taking note of Section 17 of Contract Act,1872 case of the CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 26 / 45 plaintiff is required to be appreciated. Case of plaintiff as per plaint and her deposition is to the effect that General Power of Attorney vide Ex.PW-1/1and sale deed Ex. PW-1/2 were executed in fraudulent manner. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 34 / 45 challenged by plaintiff and furthermore, in the cross-examination of plaintiff, the suggestion with regard to the presence of husband of plaintiff was put to the plaintiff and yet in the cross-examination of defendant, no efforts were made to demolish the presence of husband of plaintiff. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 35 / 45 however, husband of plaintiff was never examined as witness in the present case.

Page 37 / 45 provides that certificate of Registration shall be admissible for proving that document has been registered in the manner required under law. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 40 / 45 for the purposes of contradicting, varying, adding or subtracting its term except in the situation as contemplated in exceptions as laid down in Section 92 of Indian Evidence Act.

As held in the discussion pertaining to the determination of issue no.2 and 4 that GPA dated 19.07.1996 was validly executed, it would be appropriate to take note of the recitals stated in the Sale deed dated 19.11.1996 Ex.PW1/2 as per which plaintiff had given power of attorney to defendant no.1 and the land in dispute is sold for Rs. 4,65,000/- and amount of Rs. 99/- was received by the confirming party(defendant No.3) from vendee (defendant no.2) in cash on 14.10.1996 and sum of Rs. 4,64,901/- is to be received by the confirming party i.e defendant no.3 from defendant no.2 vide cheque no.162405 dated 14.11.1996. Plaintiff even did not file any Police complaint against any of the defendants.
75. Time gap of more than four months in executing the GPA and the sale deed and this time gap further raises the question with regard to the genuineness of the claim of plaintiff.
76. Moreover, in Dharamvir and ors vs Ved Singh (Deceased) RSA no. 20/09 dated 30.05.2011, Hon'ble Delhi High Court formulated substantial question of Law formulated as "Whether the courts below were right while dismissing the suit of appellant seeking declaration and cancellation of Sale Deed dated 30.10.1995 because the appellant did not seek the relief of cancellation of General Power of Attorney dated 12.08.1993 which according to appellant is forged and fabricated?" Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 43 / 45 cancellation of sale deed cannot be granted in the absence of relief of cancellation of GPA and in the case in hand there is no prayer for cancellation of General Power of Attorney and therefore prayer for cancellation of Sale Deed cannot be granted.

It would be apt to rely on Phoolwati vs Ram Dei and Ors 150 (2008) DLT 105 in which it was held that possession of agricultural land goes with title and revenue records are prepared in respect of agricultural land is prepared on the physical verification and aggrieved party has avail his remedy in terms of Delhi Land Reforms Act .

Page 44 / 45 that plaint discloses cause of action and raises mixed question of law and facts which merits trial as discussed above. Hence issue No.5 is decided in favour of plaintiff as against defendants.
79. Issue no.6:- Whether the suit has not been properly valued for the purpose of court fee and jurisdiction ?
OPD Suit has been correctly valued for the purposes of court fees and jurisdiction as plaintiff has valued the suit for Rs.4,65,000/- and had paid advalorem court fees of Rs. 6931/ and on the relief of injunction, plaintiff had paid fixed court fees of Rs. 13/-. Therefore, this issue is decided in favour of plaintiff as against defendants.
80. Relief.
In view of the finding recorded on issue no.1 to 4, the suit filed by plaintiff is dismissed. No order as to cost.

Page 38 / 45 husband or due to the pressure of her husband, she did not use to disclose the facts to him. This conduct of plaintiff is quite improbable to be believed upon.

66. In plaint, there is a single line averment to the effect that GPA and Sale Deed were executed in connivance with the officials of Registering Authority, however in the deposition no such facts were deposed and even due execution and registering process was not seriously challenged by the plaintiff and hence, it fortifies presumption of due execution of documents.

67. Although issue with regard to General Power of Attorney was framed, however, perusal of records would indicate that plaintiff has dropped prayer for cancellation of General Power of Attorney and in the absence of the prayer for cancellation of General Power of attorney vide Ex.PW1/1, this issue is required to be decided against the plaintiff and in favour of defendants. Reference can be had to the judgment of Dharamvir and ors vs Ved Singh (Deceased) RSA no. 20/09 dated 30.05.2011.

68. As noted earlier that in order to plead a fraud, the plaint need to disclose the material averments by giving the complete particulars as to how fraud was played. The aforementioned discussion and the analysis of plaint would also show that in strict sense, plaint does not conform to the requirement as provided in Order CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 39 / 45 VI Rule 4 CPC .
In view of the above mentioned discussion, Issue No.2 and 4 are decided against the plaintiff and in favour defendants.

69. Issue no.1:- Whether the plaintiff is entitled for declaration thus declaring the sale deed dated 14.11.1996 in favour of defendant no.2 ? OPP AND Issue no.3:- Whether any sale consideration qua sale deed dt 14.11.1996 has been paid by defendant no.3 to the plaintiff ? OPD-3 I will be taking issue no.1 and 3 for the consideration. There is a typographical error in framing issue no.1 and same should have been "Whether plaintiff is entitled for decree of declaration to the effect that sale deed dated 14.11.1996 as null and void".
Both these issues are interconnected with each other and are being disposed of together.

Before deciding on these two issues, it would be appropriate to take note of Section 91 and 92 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 which provides that when the terms of contract have been reduced to form a document then no oral evidence shall be given in proof of the terms of such contract except the document itself. Section 92 of Indian Evidence Act is an extension of Section 91 of Indian Evidence Act and it provides that no evidence of any oral agreement or statement shall be admitted between the parties to such instrument CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 40 / 45 for the purposes of contradicting, varying, adding or subtracting its term except in the situation as contemplated in exceptions as laid down in Section 92 of Indian Evidence Act.

70. As held in the discussion pertaining to the determination of issue no.2 and 4 that GPA dated 19.07.1996 was validly executed, it would be appropriate to take note of the recitals stated in the Sale deed dated 19.11.1996 Ex.PW1/2 as per which plaintiff had given power of attorney to defendant no.1 and the land in dispute is sold for Rs. 4,65,000/- and amount of Rs. 99/- was received by the confirming party(defendant No.3) from vendee (defendant no.2) in cash on 14.10.1996 and sum of Rs. 4,64,901/- is to be received by the confirming party i.e defendant no.3 from defendant no.2 vide cheque no.162405 dated 14.11.1996. It is also recorded in the recitals of sale deed that vendor (plaintiff) and the confirming party are left with no right, title or interest in the land and defendant no.2 had become the absolute owner of the land. Since sale deed was signed on behalf of plaintiff by defendant no.1. As rightly contended on behalf of defendant while relying upon the judgment of Nanjappan vs Ramsamy and Anr (2015)14 SCC 341 when terms of any contract have been reduced to a form of document no evidence of oral agreement or statement to be admitted in between the parties to any such instrument for contradicting varying and adding to or subtracting from its term.

71. Registered sale deed was executed by defendant no. 1 being the agent of plaintiff it does not lie in the mouth of principal to deny the act of an agent. Section 226 of Contract Act provides that when a contract is entered through an agent and the obligation arising out of the act done by an agent, need to be enforced in the same manner and will have the same legal consequences as if the contracts had been entered into the acts done by the principal in person

72. It is also relevant to mention that one more fact which probabilises the factum of receipt of consideration amount was the fact as the per the case set up by defendant was that original sale deed of the property (previous chain of documents vide Ex DW-2/1) was given to Mahinder Singh and who handed over the same to defendant no.2 and same is coupled with the deposition of DW-1 who also spoke about the payment of consideration.

73. Since registered general power of attorney was held to be executed by plaintiff in favour of defendant No.1 and therefore, the sale deed executed by an agent in exercise of its authority given by principal cannot be questioned and even otherwise defendants have explained and provided the complete background with regard to the receipt of consideration.

74. Plaintiff has maintained total silence with regard to the alleged conduct of defendant no 1 and it is baffling discovery of fraud CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 42 / 45 no attempt was made by the plaintiff to initiate any criminal action against defendant. It is seen from the perusal of various documents as placed on record that plaintiff took her own time in filing the present suit and same goes on to establish that plaintiff has concealed the vital facts from the Court and furthermore, no justification has been given as to why husband of plaintiff did not enter into a witness box although as claimed in the plaint that he received an information in respect of the fact that sale deed and GPA was executed in fraudulent manner. Plaintiff even did not file any Police complaint against any of the defendants.
75. Time gap of more than four months in executing the GPA and the sale deed and this time gap further raises the question with regard to the genuineness of the claim of plaintiff.

76. Moreover, in Dharamvir and ors vs Ved Singh (Deceased) RSA no. 20/09 dated 30.05.2011, Hon'ble Delhi High Court formulated substantial question of Law formulated as "Whether the courts below were right while dismissing the suit of appellant seeking declaration and cancellation of Sale Deed dated 30.10.1995 because the appellant did not seek the relief of cancellation of General Power of Attorney dated 12.08.1993 which according to appellant is forged and fabricated?" In answering the substantial question it was held Hon'ble High Court that in the absence of the relief seeking declaration of GPA null and void the relief for CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 43 / 45 cancellation of sale deed cannot be granted in the absence of relief of cancellation of GPA and in the case in hand there is no prayer for cancellation of General Power of Attorney and therefore prayer for cancellation of Sale Deed cannot be granted.

77. Plaintiff has also prayed for cancellation of mutation order dated 13.01.1997. No relief in this respect can be granted as suit land and land in dispute admittedly is an agricultural land and provisions of Delhi Land Reforms Act are applicable. In so far as the question of possession of the land in dispute is concerned, no evidence is led by plaintiff to establish that she is in possession of the suit land and furthermore, revenue record shows the name of defendant no.2 as recorded owner. It would be apt to rely on Phoolwati vs Ram Dei and Ors 150 (2008) DLT 105 in which it was held that possession of agricultural land goes with title and revenue records are prepared in respect of agricultural land is prepared on the physical verification and aggrieved party has avail his remedy in terms of Delhi Land Reforms Act .
In view of the above mentioned discussion, Issue no.1 and 3 are decided in favour of defendants and against the plaintiff.

78. Issue no.5:-Whether the suit has been filed without cause of action? OPD Bare reading of the averment as made in the plaint would reveal CS No.612639/16 Lakshmi Devi Vs. Gajender Singh and Ors. Page 44 / 45 that plaint discloses cause of action and raises mixed question of law and facts which merits trial as discussed above. Hence issue No.5 is decided in favour of plaintiff as against defendants.
79. Issue no.6:- Whether the suit has not been properly valued for the purpose of court fee and jurisdiction ?

OPD Suit has been correctly valued for the purposes of court fees and jurisdiction as plaintiff has valued the suit for Rs.4,65,000/- and had paid advalorem court fees of Rs. 6931/ and on the relief of injunction, plaintiff had paid fixed court fees of Rs. 13/-. Therefore, this issue is decided in favour of plaintiff as against defendants.
80. Relief.
In view of the finding recorded on issue no.1 to 4, the suit filed by plaintiff is dismissed. No order as to cost.
Decree sheet be prepared.
File be consigned to record room as per rules.
